sections.title: Wasting time and the love test

items.q: Where does Stephan Speaks start the 'are they wasting my time' question?
items.a: With **you**. Why are you still here? Staying because he is nice and you do not want to start over is already wasting it.

items.q: What three observable flags mean they are wasting your time?
items.a: They **will not talk**, they **will not correct** what was named, and you are **not on the same page** about the life.

items.q: What is the first sign someone deeply loves you, according to Speaks?
items.a: That **you truly love them too**. One-sided 'they love me so much, this is safe' is usually infatuation or attachment.

items.q: Why is the safe choice usually the wrong choice?
items.a: You picked someone you are **not really into** because they love you more. You cannot be what they need, and they were never what you needed.

items.q: When is showing a different side of yourself unhealthy?
items.a: When it is **not sustainable**. Five-star dates you hate, or low-text when you need daily talk. The true self comes out; they did not sign up for it.

items.q: What does 'loving in your masculine' mean?
items.a: Stay the energy they were attracted to **while you pour**. Don't become a yes-man from fear of loss. Falling in love is inevitable; collapsing is the failure.

items.q: Why does Speaks say you should keep your light on?
items.a: Openness **exposes fit faster**. Closed walls give both people a free pass to hide. Kindness was not the problem; the person was.

items.q: What is the fixer-upper actually buying you?
items.a: **Leverage** — a false sense you are the prize so they will not leave. Same leak as the unconscious helping contract.

items.q: What should you do before you decide it is time to go?
items.a: Write a **letter**, let them process, then talk on the letter. Arguing is not communication. If they still will not work, leave. Letting go is about this chapter, not always the person.
